[Paper defect — source-verified against Maths_2023_NDA1.pdf p.13: the printed data does not determine the triangle. \(\sin A=\sqrt{3}/2\) gives \(A=60^\circ\) or \(120^\circ\); both yield valid triangles satisfying every stated condition — \((60^\circ,30^\circ,90^\circ)\) with perimeter \(\sqrt{3}+3\), and \((120^\circ,30^\circ,30^\circ)\) with perimeter \(\sqrt{3}+2\), which is printed option (b). This bank retains the key matching the \(60^\circ\) branch, as issued with the paper. Under the \(120^\circ\) branch the answer is (b).]

By the sine rule \(a=2R\sin A\), so the perimeter is \(a+b+c=2R(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)\). The given condition makes the perimeter \(6\cdot\frac{\sin A+\sin B+\sin C}{3}=2(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)\). Comparing the two, \(2R=2\), so \(R=1\).

Then \(BC=a=\sqrt{3}=2\sin A\Rightarrow\sin A=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Rightarrow A=60^\circ\) or \(120^\circ\), and \(CA=b=1=2\sin B\Rightarrow\sin B=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow B=30^\circ\) (\(B=150^\circ\) is impossible, as the angle sum would exceed \(180^\circ\) in either case).

Taking \(A=60^\circ\): \(C=180^\circ-60^\circ-30^\circ=90^\circ\), so \(c=2\sin 90^\circ=2\) and the perimeter is \(\sqrt{3}+1+2=\sqrt{3}+3\). Matches option C: \(\sqrt{3}+3\).

For completeness, \(A=120^\circ\) gives \(C=30^\circ\) and \(c=2\sin 30^\circ=1\), i.e. sides \(\sqrt{3},1,1\). That is a genuine triangle — \(1+1>\sqrt{3}\), and the cosine rule returns \(a^{2}=1+1-2\cos 120^\circ=3\) — with perimeter \(\sqrt{3}+2\), option (b).

[Paper defect — source-verified against Maths_2023_NDA1.pdf p.13: the printed data does not determine the triangle. \(\sin A=\sqrt{3}/2\) gives \(A=60^\circ\) or \(120^\circ\), and both yield valid triangles satisfying every stated condition. This bank retains the key matching the \(60^\circ\) branch, as issued with the paper. Under the \(120^\circ\) branch both statements are false and the answer is (d).]

Working from the shared data directly, so this item stands on its own: by the sine rule the perimeter is \(a+b+c=2R(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)\), while the given condition makes it \(6\cdot\frac{\sin A+\sin B+\sin C}{3}=2(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)\). Comparing the two, \(R=1\).

So \(BC=\sqrt{3}=2\sin A\Rightarrow\sin A=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), and \(CA=1=2\sin B\Rightarrow\sin B=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow B=30^\circ\).

Taking \(A=60^\circ\): \(C=180^\circ-60^\circ-30^\circ=90^\circ\). Statement 1 is true, the triangle being right angled at \(C\). Statement 2 is true, since \(30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ\) are in AP with common difference \(30^\circ\). Matches option C: Both 1 and 2.

For completeness, \(A=120^\circ\) gives angles \(120^\circ,30^\circ,30^\circ\), which are neither right angled nor in AP; under that branch the answer would be (d).
